member.name: T:SHCDESE.API.Components.ModManager.LobbyModSettingsStorage
member.summary: Handles persistent storage for lobby mod settings, using encoded files stored in a dedicated folder next to each plugin's assembly.

remarks.para:
Each mod gets its own .mpsettings file stored at:
BepInEx/plugins/YourMod/LobbyModSettings/ModName.bin

The file contains a encoded Dictionary<string, byte[]> where each key is a property name and each value is the serialized property value. This allows arbitrary types (primitives, arrays, nested objects) to survive a round-trip without any type restriction.

Which properties are persisted is decided by : the two sync attributes, plus for values that are stored but never sent, minus anything marked . Undecorated properties are local UI state and are not written to disk.

member.summary: File extension for settings files.

member.summary: Absolute path to the folder where this mod's settings file lives.

member.summary: Absolute path to this mod's settings file.

member.summary: Display name of the mod, used only for logging.

member.summary: In-memory cache of the last successfully loaded or saved payload. Avoids redundant disk reads when and are called in quick succession.

member.name: M:SHCDESE.API.Components.ModManager.LobbyModSettingsStorage.#ctor(System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Creates a storage instance for a specific mod.
member.param: The full path to the plugin assembly (typically plugin.Info.Location or Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly().Location). The storage folder is created as a sibling of this file.
The mod's unique name, used as the settings filename. Must be consistent across versions: renaming it will abandon the previous settings file.

member.name: M:SHCDESE.API.Components.ModManager.LobbyModSettingsStorage.Save(System.Object)
member.summary: Saves the persisted properties of that the local player owns.

remarks.para: Each property value is serialized individually using MessagePack, then the resulting Dictionary<string, byte[]> is serialized as a whole. This means the file is always a complete snapshot — partial saves do not occur.

Because the snapshot is complete, ownership matters. On a client the live ViewModel holds values received from the host, so writing the ViewModel verbatim would overwrite this player's own settings with someone else's — even though the incoming update itself was never persisted. Host-only values are therefore skipped on a client, and the previously persisted value is carried forward so the player's own choice survives the session unchanged.

member.param: The ViewModel whose persisted properties should be written.

member.name: M:SHCDESE.API.Components.ModManager.LobbyModSettingsStorage.Load(System.Object)
member.summary:
Loads persisted settings from disk and applies them to .
A stored value is this player's own configuration, kept for when they host. Joining a lobby overwrites it in the ViewModel with the host's value, which then declines to write back.
member.remarks: Properties not present in the settings file (new properties added in a mod update) are left at their ViewModel-declared defaults. Deserialization failures for individual properties are logged and skipped so a single corrupt entry cannot prevent the rest from loading.
member.param: The ViewModel whose persisted properties should be restored.

member.summary: Serializes and writes it to . Creates the storage directory if it does not yet exist.

member.name: T:SHCDESE.API.GameMetadataManagerAPI
member.summary: Provides a persistent, key-value storage system for custom data that is automatically saved and loaded with the game. This manager is intended for tracking custom entity stats (like kill counts) or global quest states.
member.example:
This Lua script uses the metadata system to track how many kills a unit has.
-- Get the event hook local onDeathHook = Hooks:GetHook("OnUnitKilledByMelee")
-- Subscribe a function to the event onDeathHook:Subscribe(function(eventArgs) local attackerId = eventArgs.AttackingUnitId local damagedId = eventArgs.DamagedUnitId local attackerGlobalId = Unit_GetGlobalId(attackerId)
-- Get the current kill count, defaulting to 0 if it doesn't exist local killCount = tonumber(Metadata_GetInt(attackerGlobalId)) or 0 local newKillCount = killCount + 1
print("Unit id="..attackerId.."/gid="..attackerGlobalId.." has killed "..damagedId..", it now has "..newKillCount.." kills!")
-- Save the new kill count back to the metadata system Metadata_SetInt(attackerGlobalId, tostring(newKillCount))
-- NOTE: Keep in mind that you need to handle cleanup yourself. Metadata persists after unit deletion and or death. end)

member.name: T:SHCDESE.API.GameMetadataManagerAPI.EntityMetadataHolder
member.summary: The entity meta data system is responsible for storing per-entity specific metadata. Useful for keeping track of custom statistics, for example: experience, total kills, etc. The key used is the r_GlobalId entry preferrably, but can be anything.

member.name: T:SHCDESE.API.GameNetworkAPI
member.summary:
Provides the central API for all networking operations within SHCDE:SE.
Responsibilities include:
Custom packet type registration and dispatch via R3 observable streams.
Lobby-phase and in-game packet sending (channel 2, reliable).
Chat message interception and command parsing.
Player identity helpers (host check, local player ID).
Thread safety: All public methods must be called from the Unity main thread. The packet ID registry is the only section protected by a lock, as it may be touched during initialization from a background thread.

member.name: T:SHCDESE.API.GamePitchManagerAPI
member.summary: Provides a high-level API for creating, querying, and removing pitch (tar-trap) tiles.

remarks.para: Pitch tiles are stored in a flat array of up to slots embedded directly inside the TileManager struct at offset 0x2038E48. Pitch IDs are one-based: ID n is stored at array element n - 1, so ID 1 occupies the first slot. The allocator hands out 1 to MAX_PITCH_ENTRIES - 1.

In addition to the array entry, creating a pitch tile writes to three tile grids:
is OR'd into the LogicGrid.
Display bits 0x4000 and 0x2000 are cleared in MiscDisplayGrid.
The tile height is decremented by 4 (clamped to 0) in HeightGrid.
UnknownGrid2 (offset 0xA20D40) is set to 2.

member.summary: A set of common, reusable predicates for pitch queries.
member.remarks: Spatial predicates (, ) read and directly rather than delegating to the generic SpatialPredicates helper. This is necessary because SpatialPredicates calls CurrentTilePosition() which uses a fixed statement on a struct field. When the struct is already on the unmanaged heap (inside the native pitch array) and is passed as an in parameter through , the fixed expression pins a stack copy rather than the actual array element, yielding stale/garbage coordinates and causing incorrect spatial results.

member.name: M:SHCDESE.API.GamePlayerManagerAPI.SetScreenCenterPosition(System.Numerics.Vector2)
member.summary: Sets the camera raw position directly in Unity World Space.
member.param: The target Unity World Space coordinate. This is NOT a game tile coordinate.
member.remarks: This function operates on the engine internal camera coordinate system. It does not account for isometric projection, map rotation, or terrain height. Using game tile coordinates (e.g., 400, 400) with this function will result in unpredictable camera movement as the coordinates will be misinterpreted. It is preserved for specific low-level use cases or for restoring a previously saved raw camera position. For general use, call instead.

member.name: M:SHCDESE.API.GamePlayerManagerAPI.SetScreenCenterToTilePosition(System.Numerics.Vector2)
member.summary: Moves the camera to center the view on a specific local game tile coordinate. This is the recommended function for camera positioning.
member.param: A Vector2 containing the target local tile coordinates (e.g., X=400, Y=400 on a 400x400 map).
member.remarks:
This function acts as a translator, converting human-readable grid coordinates into the complex world coordinates required by the camera. It should be used instead of SetScreenCenterPosition, which expects raw camera coordinates. The conversion process is as follows:
1. Takes a Local Tile Coordinate (the game logical grid).
2. Converts it to an internal Isometric Tilemap Coordinate, accounting for map rotation.
3. Calculates the base Unity World Position for that tile.
4. Adjusts the World Position Y-axis based on the tile terrain height.
5. Passes the final, calculated World Position to the camera controller.

member.name: M:SHCDESE.API.GamePlayerManagerAPI.GetScreenCenterTilePosition
member.summary: Gets the local game tile coordinate that is currently at the center of the screen.
member.returns: A representing the local tile coordinate (e.g., X and Y) at the screen center. Returns if the required game instances are not available or if a valid tile cannot be resolved.
member.remarks: This function performs the inverse transformation from screen space to the game local tile coordinate system. It works by querying the game internal method with the screen's center point. This process accounts for the current camera position, zoom level, map rotation, and isometric terrain height, ensuring the returned coordinate matches the same system used by .

member.name: F:SHCDESE.API.GameTileManagerAPI.MapRowLookupTable
member.summary: A pointer to the games internal map row lookup table (LUT) used to convert 2D tile coordinates (X, Y) into a 1D array index.

remarks.para:
Theory:
The game uses an isometric map projection, not a simple top-down grid. Due to the staggered, diamond-like layout of an isometric map, the standard formula for calculating a tile's index (`index = y * width + x`) is not applicable. Calculating the correct offset for each row on-the-fly would be computationally expensive and too slow for real-time access.

Functionality:
To solve this performance issue, the game engine pre-calculates the starting index for every single map row (from Y=0 to Y=799). These starting indices are stored in this lookup table. This turns a complex geometric calculation into a single, highly-performant memory lookup, which is a critical optimization for all tile data access.

Usage in Formulas:
This table is used in functions like with the formula: index = tileX + MapRowLookupTable[3 * tileY] In this formula, `MapRowLookupTable[3 * tileY]` instantly retrieves the starting index of the desired row `tileY`. The `tileX` value is then simply added as an offset to pinpoint the exact tile within that row.

Memory Layout and the `* 3` Multiplier:
The multiplication by 3 indicates that the table is not a simple array of integers. Instead, it is an array of structures, where each structure contains 3 integers (12 bytes) for each map row. The formula `[3 * tileY]` is pointer arithmetic that accesses the first integer in the 3-integer block for the given `tileY`, which is the row's starting index. The other two integers per row are used for other internal engine purposes, which are not as of yet documented.

member.name: T:SHCDESE.API.GameTranslateAPI
member.summary: Provides an API for interacting with and overriding the game's text translation system. Supports localization files (crusader.txt format) and temporary/permanent overrides.
member.remarks: This singleton class allows scripts to dynamically change in-game text. It works by intercepting the game's internal `Translate.lookUpText` methods. When the game requests a piece of text, this API first checks if a custom override exists. If so, it returns the custom text; otherwise, it allows the original game function to proceed. Supports both permanent overrides (cleared on map unload) and temporary overrides (cleared manually).

member.name: M:SHCDESE.API.GameTribeManagerAPI.GetUnits(System.Int32,System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32})
member.summary: Retrieves all unit IDs belonging to the specified tribe by scanning its membership bitfield.
member.remarks:
The tribe stores its members in a flat bitset of 625 consecutive words (10,000 bits total), where each set bit's absolute position across the array directly encodes a unit ID. Word n covers unit IDs n*16 through n*16+15.
Scanning stops early once members have been found, avoiding a full 625-word traversal for small tribes.
member.param: The ID of the tribe whose units should be retrieved.
A caller-provided list that will be populated with the unit IDs of all members of the tribe. The list is not cleared before population; existing entries are preserved.
member.returns: if the tribe was found and the results list was successfully populated; if no tribe with the given could be located.

member.name: T:SHCDESE.API.GameTriggerManager
member.summary: A high-performance system for detecting when game entities enter or exit defined areas (triggers).
member.remarks: This manager uses a spatial partitioning grid to efficiently check entity positions against trigger zones. Instead of a brute-force check of every entity against every trigger each frame, it drastically reduces the number of checks by only considering triggers in the same grid cell as the entity. This class should be updated once per game frame via the method.

member.name: M:SHCDESE.API.GameTriggerManager.Update
member.summary: Executes one update tick of the trigger system. This should be called once per game frame.
member.remarks:
This method performs three main tasks:
Check Phase: Iterates through all active game units, determines their grid cell, and checks them against the small list of potential triggers in that cell. It identifies all "OnEnter" events during this phase.
State Update: It builds a complete set of all entities that are inside any trigger during the current frame.
Exit Detection: It compares the current frames state with each triggers previous frames state to efficiently find all "OnExit" events.

member.name: M:SHCDESE.API.GameXAMLManagerAPI.TryGetSettingProperty(System.Object,System.String,System.Reflection.PropertyInfo@)
member.summary:
Resolves on and reports whether that property is a setting at all.
It is one if routes it anywhere, to the network or to disk. Everything else is presentation state: undecorated properties, and names that do not resolve to a public instance property. Both are rejected here, before any networking or storage decision is made.
member.param: The ViewModel that raised the change notification.
The notified property name. An empty name is the "every property changed" convention and names no single setting to route, so it is not treated as a settings change.
The resolved property, or null when this returns false.
member.returns: true if the property resolved and is synchronised, persisted, or both.

member.name: M:SHCDESE.API.GameXAMLManagerAPI.IsLocallyAuthoritative(System.Reflection.PropertyInfo)
member.summary:
Determines whether the local player is allowed to originate a change to .
Returns false only for properties changed by a non-host inside a networked session. Per-player properties are always locally authoritative, as is everything in singleplayer.
Callers pass an already-resolved setting property; presentation state and unresolvable names are filtered out by before authorisation is considered.

member.name: M:SHCDESE.API.GameXAMLManagerAPI.BroadcastSettingChange(System.String,System.Object,System.Reflection.PropertyInfo)
member.summary:
Evaluates whether a changed property should be broadcast to other players, then serialises and sends it if so.
Routing rules:
: any player may broadcast their own value.
: only the host may broadcast.
No attribute: not synced; such properties never reach this method.
Sync attribution is settled before any networking state is consulted, so a property that is not synchronised in the first place is never reported as an attempted sync.

member.summary: Provides a central notification point for when the primary game library (CrusaderDE.dll) has been loaded into memory.
member.remarks: This singleton class is a cornerstone of the script extender initialization process. Its primary purpose is to fire the event at the earliest possible moment after the target DLL is mapped into the process memory. Other managers, particularly those that need to apply detours or perform memory scanning (AOB), must subscribe to this event to ensure they only execute their logic after the memory they depend on is available and valid.

member.name: T:SHCDESE.API.ModSaveDataAPI
member.summary: Provides an extensible API for mods to save and load custom data within the Map Archive system. Mods can register handlers to persist data across save/load cycles with control over when data is written. Archives are created automatically on-demand when mods need to save data.
member.remarks:
This system distinguishes between: - Save files (.sav) - game saves during gameplay - Map files (.map) - maps being edited or saved in the map editor
Mods can choose to save data: - Only for save files (gameplay saves) - For all saves including map editor saves - With custom logic based on the save context

This method is the entry point for all game-specific initialization. It runs within a loader lock, so it must execute quickly. It is responsible for finding game globals, applying all game-function detours, and setting up all high-level APIs like the Lua manager.

member.remarks: This static class is responsible for finding specific functions within the game's memory using Array-of-Bytes (AOB) scanning and redirecting their execution to custom C# implementations. member.name: F:SHCDESE.EventAPI.AIR3EventHooks.OnAIQueryBuildHovelEventArgs
member.summary:
Fired when the game ai checks if it should build a new hovel or not
Default behavior:
The AI will block hovel construction when the player already has more than 12 civilian housing spaces and at least one of the following conditions is true:
Total population is below available housing capacity.
Current idle peasant count is 5 or greater.
Average idle peasant count is 5 or greater.
Current popularity is below 5000.
Returns true only for MAPPER_HOVEL; all other building types return false.

member.name: T:SHCDESE.EventAPI.BuildingR3EventHooks
member.summary: Provides static R3EventHook fields for subscribing to various building-related events in the game.
member.remarks: This class centralizes all events tied to building actions, such as creation, destruction, damage, and state changes. Modders can subscribe to these hooks to execute custom logic when these game events occur. Each event is fired with a 'Pre' phase (before the original game logic) and a 'Post' phase (after).

member.name: F:SHCDESE.EventAPI.BuildingR3EventHooks.OnIsBuildingAdjacentToOther
member.summary: Fired when the game checks if a building is being placed adjacent to another of the same type.
member.remarks: This event allows for modifying the parameters of the adjacency check or overriding its result. It is commonly used by the game for buildings like quarries or farms that have placement restrictions based on proximity to others. In the 'Post' phase, the original function's result is available in , which can be modified.

member.name: F:SHCDESE.EventAPI.BuildingR3EventHooks.OnGranarySpawnChicken
member.summary: Fired just before a Granary spawns a chicken.
member.remarks: This event allows for changing the position or the type of "chimp" (typically a chicken) being spawned.

member.name: F:SHCDESE.EventAPI.BuildingR3EventHooks.OnKeepSpawnPeasant
member.summary: Fired when a Keep is about to spawn a peasant.
member.remarks: This event intercepts the peasant spawning logic that originates from the player's Keep. It allows for modification of the peasant's spawn location and owner, or to cancel the spawn entirely. The actual unit spawning is handled by the unit manager, and this event acts as a high-level trigger.

member.name: F:SHCDESE.EventAPI.BuildingR3EventHooks.OnBuildingSpawn
member.summary: Fired when a core building object is spawned into the game world.
member.remarks: This is a low-level event that triggers after a building's data structure is initialized but before it's fully integrated. It's useful for tracking the creation of any building and getting its ID immediately. The building ID is available in the 'Post' phase via . This event is triggered by higher-level actions like .

member.name: F:SHCDESE.EventAPI.BuildingR3EventHooks.OnBuildWall
member.summary: Fired when a player builds a wall or a tower.
member.remarks: This event allows for intercepting the creation of defensive structures. You can modify the start and end coordinates, the owner, or the type of wall being built.

member.name: F:SHCDESE.EventAPI.BuildingR3EventHooks.OnBuildingTileTakeDamage
member.summary: Fired when a building's tile takes damage from any source.
member.remarks: This is the primary event for handling building damage. It allows for modifying the amount of damage dealt, redirecting it, or making buildings invincible by setting damage to zero. The source of the damage (player ID) is also available.

member.name: F:SHCDESE.EventAPI.BuildingR3EventHooks.OnBuildStructure
member.summary: Fired when a player attempts to build a complete structure (prefab), including resource deduction and placement checks.
member.remarks: This is a high-level event that represents the entire building placement process. It triggers before .

member.name: F:SHCDESE.EventAPI.BuildingR3EventHooks.OnBuildingBulldoze
member.summary: Fired when a building is bulldozed by the player.
member.remarks: This event is specific to the "bulldoze" action, which typically returns resources to the player.

member.summary: Fired when a building is deleted through a direct, low-level function call.
member.remarks: This event is more general than and can be triggered by game scripts or other internal logic. It signifies the immediate removal of a building from memory.

member.remarks: This event allows for direct manipulation of resource flow into storage buildings. You can change the amount of the good, the type of good, or the target storage building's capacity.

member.name: F:SHCDESE.EventAPI.BuildingR3EventHooks.OnPlacementValidation
member.summary: Fired during the validation phase of building placement, before any resources are spent.
member.remarks: This is a powerful event that allows for the creation of custom building placement rules. By setting to true, you can use to either allow or deny the placement, overriding the game's default logic entirely.

member.name: F:SHCDESE.EventAPI.BuildingR3EventHooks.OnBuildingRefund
member.summary: Fired when a building is refunded as a result of a player self-bulldoze.

remarks.para:
The final refunded resource amounts are determined by two compounding factors:
Percentage — passed into the underlying c_game_refund_building native function. Modifying in the phase will change the percentage forwarded to the native function.
Per-resource multipliers — applied by a secondary inline intercept after the native function computes its base amounts. These are controlled by , , , , , which each default to DEFAULT_BUILDING_REFUND_MULTIPLIER (0.5).
The effective refund for each resource is therefore: buildingCost * (Percentage / 100f) * ResourceRefundMultiplier.

member.name: F:SHCDESE.EventAPI.PlayerR3EventHooks.OnPlayerCalculateExpenditure
member.summary: Fired every game tick for each active player when their donation/bribe expenditure is calculated and added to a monthly accumulator. Only fires when is HugeDonation, BigDonation, or SmallDonation. This fires many times per month, the gold is not deducted yet at this point.

member.name: F:SHCDESE.EventAPI.PlayerR3EventHooks.OnPlayerTaxIncome
member.summary: Fired once per month per active player during the settlement tick, after the accumulated tax income and donation expenses have been normalized (/10) and applied to the player's gold (r_TotalGoodsGold). At this point the gold has already moved, income has been added and expenses have been subtracted (floored at zero). Provides the final settled income amount, expense amount, and the player's resulting gold total.

member.name: F:SHCDESE.EventAPI.PlayerR3EventHooks.OnPlayerTaxExpenditure
member.summary: Same as but for expenditures (bribes) only

member.name: M:SHCDESE.Extensions.AudioClipExtensions.LoadAudioClipFromBytes(System.Byte[])
member.summary: Identifies an audio format from a byte array and creates an AudioClip. NOTE: ONLY CALL THIS FROM THE UNITY MAIN THREAD.
member.param: The byte array containing the audio file data (WAV or OGG).
member.returns: An AudioClip, or null if the format is unsupported or decoding fails.

member.name: M:SHCDESE.Extensions.AudioClipExtensions.LoadOggFromBytes(System.Byte[])
member.summary: Decodes a byte array of OGG Vorbis audio data and creates an AudioClip.

member.name: M:SHCDESE.Extensions.AudioClipExtensions.LoadWavFromBytes(System.Byte[])
member.summary: Loads a WAV byte array and returns an AudioClip representing it.
member.param: The wav file.
member.returns: Created AudioClip

remarks.para: Supports 16-bit PCM WAV files at 44100 Hz with either 1 (mono) or 2 (stereo) channels.
Unity's AudioClip expects interleaved samples for multi-channel audio, which matches the standard WAV layout (L, R, L, R, ...), so no re-interleaving is required for stereo.

member.summary: Adds a specified amount of a good to the building's local storage, clamping at the given capacity.

The type of good to add.
The amount to add.
Optional capacity override. If null, the building's r_MaxGoodStackAmount is used.
member.remarks: This method updates both the specific good's amount in the local storage array and syncs the r_CurrentGoodStackAmount. It will also set the r_LocalStorageGoodType if the new amount is greater than zero. This function does not visually update.

member.summary: Removes a specified amount of a good from the building's local storage by adding a negative value.
member.param: The instance to modify.
The type of good to remove.
The amount to remove. This value is expected to be negative. For example, to remove 10, pass -10.
member.remarks: The final amount is clamped at zero. This method updates the r_CurrentGoodStackAmount and resets the r_LocalStorageGoodType to if the storage becomes empty. This function does not visually update.

member.summary:
Scans an object instance and registers all of its methods (and properties) decorated with .

member.summary:

If the type carries a the exported Lua name will be <Prefix>_<MemberName>; otherwise the attribute name is used verbatim.

The class whose static members will be registered.
Reflection flags used during the member search.

member.name: M:SHCDESE.Extensions.LuaExtensions.RegisterManagedValue(NLua.Lua,System.String,System.Object,System.Reflection.BindingFlags)
member.summary:
Registers a managed-value object under a fixed Lua prefix by exposing its Push, Pop, Set, and GetValue methods automatically.
The resulting Lua globals will be:
<luaPrefix>_Push(value)
<luaPrefix>_Pop()
<luaPrefix>_Set(value)
<luaPrefix>_GetValue()
Any methods not found on are skipped with a warning.
member.param: The Lua state.
The prefix used when building the Lua function names, e.g. "WoodCost".

member.name: T:SHCDESE.Interop.Enums.ChoreType
member.summary:
The game uses a "Chore" system to is responsible for game state changes, specifically to keep multiplayer games in sync with the tick system. There is a individual enum value for specific tasks, where each enum has a custom "packet" that contains metadata that the game will interpret alongside other clients if in a active multiplayer session.
Many of these also get used by gGamestateHandlers in connection with c_game_queue_chore There are many more of these chore types, but currently almost none of them are mapped.
28 might be castle placement 15 might be building placement

member.name: F:SHCDESE.Interop.Enums.ChoreType.SyncManifest
member.summary: Periodically broadcast by the scheduling/authoritative side every gSyncIntervalTicks ticks. Contains a target-tick checkpoint, a running sequence number, and a list of up to 25 unique chore IDs that this client has queued and expects every other client to have received by that tick. Used purely for desync detection/enforcement, receiving clients check their local chore ring buffer against this manifest and will stall (up to a 3-second timeout, after which they force-proceed and log "SyncEvent - Forced run") if any listed chore hasn't arrived yet. Does not carry gameplay data itself. INT32: TargetTick INT32: ChoreIdCount (capped at 25) INT32: SequenceNumber INT32[ChoreIdCount]: UniqueChoreIds [UNCONFIRMED]

Popularity effects are applied separately and not part of this enum's logic.

member.remarks: Use this enumeration to control whether a unit moves in coordination with the tribe or independently. 'Unknown' indicates that the movement type has not been specified.

member.name: T:SHCDESE.Interop.GamePitchDescriptor
member.summary: Represents a single pitch (tar/fire-trap) entry as it exists in native memory. The struct is exactly 20 bytes and maps directly onto the game's pitch array, which begins at TileManager + 0x2038E48 with a stride of 20 bytes per slot.
member.remarks:
Field layout reverse-engineered from c_game_player_build_pitch_ditch:
+0x00 uint32 GlobalId - gGlobalIdsUsed assigned at creation +0x04 int16 OwnerId - player who placed the pitch +0x06 uint16 TileX - tile X coordinate +0x08 uint16 TileY - tile Y coordinate +0x0A uint16 RandomSeed - visual noise seed (gRandomShort+1) +0x0C uint32 State - flags/state, 0 = normal +0x10 uint32 _padding - reserved
A slot is considered free when the sentinel word at PitchArrayBase + 0x18 + stride*(id-1) is zero (game's own scan logic).

member.name: T:SHCDESE.Interop.GameTileManagerView
member.summary: Provides a structured, safe view over the raw memory buffer of the game's tile manager. This is not complete, and is likely missing plenty of existing grids that have yet to be found.
member.remarks: This class maps the game's contiguous block of memory for tile data into distinct, type-safe properties. Each property corresponds to a specific grid of data for the entire map (e.g., tile height, ownership, properties). Accessing tile data through this class is neccessary due to the TileManager being too large for simple C# structures (1MB limit)

member.name: T:SHCDESE.Interop.Query.RefAction`1
member.summary: Callback invoked for each matched element.
member.param: The matched element, by reference.

The one-based game ID when invoked via GameStructQuery{T}.ForEach, or the raw zero-based slot index when invoked via GameStructQuery{T}.ForEachIndex. Which one you get is determined by the method you call, so prefer ForEach unless you are indexing a span directly.

member.name: T:SHCDESE.Interop.Query.GameStructQuery`1
member.summary: A lightweight, allocation-free query over a native game struct array.

remarks.para: ID convention. The game stores entities in flat, zero-indexed native arrays, but every public accessor in the script extender (TryGetBuildingById, TryGetUnitById, TryGetTribeById, ...) takes a one-based game ID and internally resolves it as _array[id - 1]. The corresponding IsValidId checks reject 0.

To keep the whole surface consistent, everything this query type hands back to a caller is a one-based game ID. Members that deliberately expose the raw zero-based slot index are named explicitly (, , ).
The rule of thumb: id == index + 1. Anything named ...Id... is safe to pass straight into a TryGet...ById method; anything named ...Index... is only valid for direct span/array indexing.

member.param: The list to be cleared and filled with game IDs.

remarks.para: Every value written to is slot index + 1 and can be passed directly to the matching TryGet...ById accessor without any further adjustment.

member.name: M:SHCDESE.Lua.LuaBuildingAPI.GetAllBuildingIds(NLua.LuaTable)
member.summary: Finds all building IDs on the map, with optional filters.
member.param:
Optional. A Lua table containing query parameters:
state: Filters for buildings in a specific (e.g., `eAliveState.IsAlive`).
buildingType: Filters for a specific type of building using the enum.
relationship: Filters buildings based on their allegiance to a player, using .
povPlayer: The player ID to use for the 'relationship' check.
member.returns: An array of one-based building IDs for all buildings that match the criteria. Each value can be passed directly to any Building_* function that takes a buildingId.
member.example:
The following Lua code finds all active Granaries owned by Player 1.
local granaries = Building_Query({ state = eAliveState.IsAlive, buildingType = eStructs.STRUCT_GRANARY, relationship = ePlayerRelationship.Allied, povPlayer = 1 })
print("Player 1 has " .. #granaries .. " granaries.")

member.summary: Manages the lifecycle of the NLua state for map scripting and per-lord AI scripting.

The manager is a singleton that subscribes to map load/unload events and coordinates:
Creating and tearing down the shared state on map transitions.
Executing the map's init.lua entry point at the correct lifecycle phase.
Running per-lord AI scripts inside isolated table environments.
Initialize the event subscriptions by calling once during plugin startup.

member.name: M:SHCDESE.Lua.LuaManager.TryCallUnload
member.summary: Attempts to call the unload() function in the active Lua state, giving scripts a chance to clean up before the state is destroyed. Exceptions are swallowed since the state may already be partially invalid.

member.name: M:SHCDESE.Lua.LuaManager.TryUnload
member.summary: Tears down and disposes the active Lua state and all associated lord environments. Clears network packet hooks and the UI layer.

member.name: M:SHCDESE.Lua.LuaManager.InitLordAIs
member.summary: Initializes all pending lord AI scripts by loading each one into an isolated Lua table environment and calling ai_init(playerId) if it is defined.
member.remarks: Each lord's environment uses its own table with _G as the __index fallback, ensuring lords share access to global Script Extender APIs without polluting each other's scope.

member.name: M:SHCDESE.Lua.LuaManager.UnloadLordAIs
member.summary: Clears all active lord AI environments and pending registrations from the Lua state. Called during map unload.

member.name: M:SHCDESE.Lua.LuaManager.RegisterAssetMod(System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Registers an Asset Mod as a candidate for per-map Lua execution. Must be called during plugin startup (before maps load). If a Lua state is already active, the mod is initialised immediately.
member.param: The mod's unique GUID (used as the global table name, e.g. MyMod).
Absolute path to Scripts/init.lua.
Absolute path to the mod root (used for sandboxed file I/O).

member.name: M:SHCDESE.Lua.LuaManager.InitAssetMods(SHCDESE.Lua.LuaManager.LuaLoadMode)
member.summary: Initialises all pending asset mod Lua scripts. Each mod receives its own isolated table environment (with _G as the __index fallback), mirrors the Lord AI pattern, and has its I/O sandbox rooted at its own directory.
member.remarks:
Called from after the map script but before Lord AI init. Entry points called per mod:
mod_init() - fresh map start
mod_load(false) - save game loaded
mod_load(true) - map editor opened
member.param: The map lifecycle mode, used to select the correct entry point.

member.name: M:SHCDESE.Lua.LuaManager.UnloadAssetMods
member.summary: Calls mod_unload() on every active asset mod environment and then removes the environments from the Lua state. Called during map unload.

member.summary: Finds all pitch slot IDs within a rectangular area, with optional filters.
member.param: A Lua table with keys: x, y, width, height (required), and optionally owner, relationship (), povPlayer.

example.code: -- All enemy pitch in area local ids = Pitch_FindInRect({ x=100, y=100, width=50, height=50, relationship=ePlayerRelationship.Enemy, povPlayer=1 }) for i = 1, ids.Length do print("Enemy pitch id: " .. ids[i-1]) end

member.returns: An array of one-based pitch IDs that match the criteria. Each value can be passed directly to any Pitch_* function that takes a pitchId.

example.code: -- All allied pitch within 20 tiles of a point local ids = Pitch_FindInSphere({ x=400, y=400, radius=20, relationship=ePlayerRelationship.Allied, povPlayer=1 }) print("Nearby allied pitch count: " .. ids.Length)

member.name: M:SHCDESE.Lua.LuaPitchAPI.GetAllPitchIds(NLua.LuaTable)
member.summary: Returns all pitch slot IDs on the map, with optional filters.

-- All pitch on map local allIds = Pitch_GetAllIds()

member.name: M:SHCDESE.Lua.LuaTileAPI.GetTilesInRect(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Retrieves an array of TileIDs for all tiles within a specified rectangular area. Exposed to Lua.
member.param: The starting X coordinate of the rectangle.
The starting Y coordinate of the rectangle.
The width of the rectangle.
The height of the rectangle.
member.returns: An array of integer TileIDs within the specified rectangle.
member.example:
The following Lua code gets all tile IDs in a 10x10 box, prints them and sets their height to 20.
local tileIds = Tile_FindInRect(400, 400, 10, 10) for i=1, tileIds.Length, 1 do print("Found tile ID: " .. tileIds[i-1]) SetTileHeight(tileIds[i-1], 20) end

member.name: M:SHCDESE.Lua.LuaTileAPI.GetTilesInRange(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Retrieves an array of TileIDs for all tiles within a circular range of a central point. Exposed to Lua.
member.param: The X coordinate of the center point.
The Y coordinate of the center point.
The radius of the circle (in tiles).
member.returns: An array of integer TileIDs within the specified range.
member.example:
The following Lua code gets all tile IDs within a 5-tile radius of a point.
local tileIds = Tile_FindInRange(400, 400, 5) print("Found " .. tileIds.Length .. " tiles in range.")

member.name: M:SHCDESE.Lua.LuaTileAPI.GetRandomInRect(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,NLua.LuaFunction)
member.summary: Gets a random tile within a rectangle, optionally filtering by a Lua function.
member.param: Top-left X.
Top-left Y.
Width.
Height.
Optional Lua function(tileId) -> bool. If provided, the tile must return true to be picked.
member.returns: The selected x, y coordinates in a . Returns default if not found.

example.code:
-- Get any random tile local pos = Tile_GetRandomInRect(10, 10, 20, 20) print(pos.x, pos.y)
-- Get random tile that is NOT Rock (Condition) local pos2 = Tile_GetRandomInRect(10, 10, 20, 20, function(id) return Tile_HasPropertyFlag(id, eTilePropertyFlag.ImpassableEdge) end)

member.name: T:SHCDESE.LUA.LuaAssemblyGlobalProxy
member.summary:
A type-erased Lua-facing proxy for a or .
NLua passes all Lua numbers as double, which means calling gSomeCap:Push(4) from Lua would fail with "Invalid arguments" when the underlying generic method expects a byte, int, etc.
This proxy exposes only plain double parameters to NLua, converts them to the correct underlying type at runtime via , and forwards the call to the real managed wrapper.

member.name: T:SHCDESE.UI.ComboBoxDropDownFix
member.summary:
Works around a Noesis popup placement issue that makes a drop-down open and immediately close again.
When the drop-down does not fit below the ComboBox, Noesis nudges the popup back into the view bounds, which can place it directly underneath the cursor. The mouse-release of the very same click then lands on a popup item, selecting it and closing the drop-down. The symptom is position dependent: the same ComboBox behaves normally near the top of a view and misbehaves further down.
The fix is to shrink MaxDropDownHeight to the space actually available below the control just before the drop-down opens, so the popup always stays below the click point and is never repositioned. The value authored in XAML is remembered and used as an upper bound, so this only ever shrinks a drop-down, never grows one.

member.name: T:System.Runtime.CompilerServices.ModuleInitializerAttribute
member.summary: Used to indicate to the compiler that a method should be called in its containing module's initializer.
member.remarks:
When one or more valid methods with this attribute are found in a compilation, the compiler will emit a module initializer which calls each of the attributed methods.
Certain requirements are imposed on any method targeted with this attribute: - The method must be `static`. - The method must be an ordinary member method, as opposed to a property accessor, constructor, local function, etc. - The method must be parameterless. - The method must return `void`. - The method must not be generic or be contained in a generic type. - The method's effective accessibility must be `internal` or `public`.
The specification for module initializers in the .NET runtime can be found here: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/design/specs/Ecma-335-Augments.md#module-initializer
